messages:
Mia Chen: Quick q — for the config audit export we discussed in the last sync: are we planning to include full pre/post payloads in the NDJSON export by default?
Samir Patel: Short answer: no, not by default. We need to be careful about size & PII.
Lucas Reed: +1. Full payloads blow up storage and make exports heavy. I was thinking we store a compact diff and a pointer to full snapshot if needed.
Anya Ivanova: What does 'pointer' look like? signed URL? internal blob id? retention implications?
Kevin Brooks: Signed URL for hosted, blob id for private deployments. But retention policy still applies — we can't keep full snapshots forever without controls.
Mia Chen: Makes sense. Customers will ask "who changed what" — diffs must be human-readable and include metadata (actor, IP, rule id).
Samir Patel: Agreed. Proposal: export schema lines = {meta, change_type, change_summary, diff_snippet, full_snapshot_url?}. Default export omits full_snapshot_url unless user toggles "include_snapshots" param.
Lucas Reed: That feels reasonable. For compliance use-cases they will want full context; but include_snapshots should require an extra grant and count against export quota.
Anya Ivanova: Export quota — do we gate by rows or bytes? Bytes is safer (prevents someone asking for giant binary snapshots).
Kevin Brooks: Bytes + API rate limit. Also retention settings: default 90d for full snapshots, 365d for compact events. Customers can request custom retention for Private/Dedicated through config.
Mia Chen: For the console UX, how do we surface "who changed X" inline? Popover with diff + link to export? Or inline timeline?
Samir Patel: Timeline is nice but can be noisy. I'd prefer compact timeline with expand to diff and an "export context" button.
Lucas Reed: Implementation detail — our change events already capture old/new as JSON in the DB. We can diff server-side with a small util and store the diff_snippet. Code example: ```python
def compact_diff(old, new):
    # shallow-diff fields, return max 2 keys with context
    ...
```
Anya Ivanova: Need to prove diffs are deterministic & stable for replay. Also include object version id so audits are unambiguous.
Kevin Brooks: Ops note: when generating signed URLs for snapshots, tie expiry to retention policy so the URL disappears when snapshot is purged.
Mia Chen: Good call. Also we need to document export formats clearly for SOC2 reviewers. Add fields: actor.email, actor.id, auth_method, region, change_ts, route_id, route_name.
Samir Patel: One more: redaction. We must run a redaction pipeline over snapshots before making them downloadable for hosted. For private, we give an opt-in config to skip redaction (enterprise only).
Lucas Reed: How about searching exports? If a customer requests exports filtered by actor or route, we should support server-side filters. But that changes our indexing & query cost.
Anya Ivanova: Indexes for actor and route_id only — that should cover most compliance queries. Full-text search over snapshots is expensive and not needed initially.
Kevin Brooks: Quotas: free tier limited to 1GB/month export bytes, paid tiers get higher caps, and for large one-off exports we route to an async job and email a link when ready.
Mia Chen: UX flow: 1) user selects time range & filters 2) preview row count & estimated bytes 3) confirm export (cost estimate) 4) async job. Everyone agree?
Samir Patel: Yes. Display estimate and require a confirmation for >100MB.
Lucas Reed: Edge case: on Private deployments with on-prem snapshots, we should support local archive-only export (no signed URLs). Add a flag "local_archive=true".
Anya Ivanova: Also need to record export events in the audit trail itself (who exported what). Otherwise you can't prove someone accessed the snapshots.
Kevin Brooks: Good call. Export actions are an event type with their own meta: export_id, initiator, scope, filters, byte_count, completed_ts.
Mia Chen: Ops/billing: export bytes should increment the usage meter immediately when job completes, not on job enqueue.
Samir Patel: Security: if export contains workspace-scoped secrets, we must ensure KMS policy prevents cross-tenant leak. Redaction helps but KMS protects encrypted snapshots.
deploy-bot: Job 2378 queued for export request by @Mia. ETA ~2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Mia Chen: Thanks bot. Ok action items: Samir/Lucas implement compact diff + include_snapshots flag; Kevin & Ops draft retention defaults and quota limits; Anya & Product write UX copy and preview flow; I'll draft SOC2 export schema docs.
Samir Patel: I'll PR the API param: `?include_snapshots=true&local_archive=true` and add server-side guard for enterprise-only.
Lucas Reed: I'll add `diff_snippet` generation and `snapshot_url` field to the NDJSON schema.
Anya Ivanova: I'll mock the UI & send a Figma link later.
Kevin Brooks: I'll add quota enforcement and audit event for exports.
Mia Chen: Perfect. Follow-up sync Friday 10am to freeze defaults. :thumbsup:
